tagline: A Delaware river road that turns off through the fields.
intro: The byway is seventeen miles of Route 611, Little Creek Road and the Belvidere Highway between Easton and Riverton, with the Delaware and Little Martin's Creek for a backdrop. Below Martins Creek, Route 611 keeps to the west bank of the Delaware through Forks Township, past woods and homes by the river. At Martins Creek it turns away from the water, and from there the byway reaches Riverton through farm country.
The country around Martins Creek was called Flatfield in the 1800s for its level ground, then Martinsville by the Civil War, and only later Martin's Creek.

moments.title: Martins Creek
moments.text: James Martin, who came around 1747, ran a gristmill here, and in 1939 the exiled Russian prime minister Alexander Kerensky was married in the village.

moments.title: Riverton–Belvidere Bridge
moments.text: The first bridge across to Belvidere, New Jersey went up here in 1836, and when the floods of 1903 took it, it was rebuilt the next year with steel in place of wood.
